Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & throughput guarantees — measurement methodology (details)

Lena / Karthik — diving into the measurement methodology you can expect from us. I kept it pragmatic so your infra team can reproduce it if desired.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Throughput guarantees are specified at pool-level: we commit to sustained tokens/sec and concurrent request throughput for a configured pool size (e.g., 4xA100 equiv).
- Latency SLOs are defined as p50/p95/p99 measured over a 1-minute rolling window for burst SLOs and a 1-hour rolling window for sustained SLOs.

Measurement procedure (canonical):
1) Test harness: we recommend our dedicated load harness (we can share a container) or an equivalent of wrk/vegeta configured to send realistic request payloads (including prompt lengths, avg tokens out).
2) Warm-up: a 20-minute warm-up that mimics your production prefix cache population. Warm-up is mandatory and excluded from SLA calculations. Warm-up is "KV cache warm" for generation-style workloads; for stateless embeddings/rerank we use a 5-minute warm-up.
3) Workload profile: provide us with representative traffic traces (timestamps, prompt length distribution, model variant, temperature) or we run a replay with synthetic distributions you approve. If no traces, we default to the 95th percentile of your provided estimate.
4) Metrics collected: tokens/sec (aggregate pool), requests/sec (aggregate), GPU utilization per instance, queue depth, and per-request latency percentiles at model decode completion. We also record token-generation time and server-side queue latency separately.
5) SLO pass criteria: for sustained SLOs (1-hour window), we require p95 latency <= X ms and aggregate tokens/sec >= committed rate for at least 95% of one-hour windows over a 24-hour run. For burst windows (1-minute), p95 must meet the burst threshold for 95% of 1-minute windows in a separate 2-hour burst test. (Numeric thresholds depend on model & pool sizing; see example below.)

Example thresholds (4xA100 equivalent, gpt-open-xx):
- Sustained: aggregate >= 75k tokens/sec, p95 latency <= 220 ms, p99 <= 420 ms
- Burstable: short bursts up to 120k tokens/sec for 90 seconds, p95 <= 340 ms during bursts
- Requests/sec: guarantees expressed as concurrent user slots; default mapping is 1 request = average 1.2k tokens for your workload, so 75k tokens/sec ~= 62 rps sustained.

Considerations:
- Quantized/FP16 model variants will have different throughput; SLA ties to a named model artifact (e.g., gpt-open-xx:fp16-q4_0).
- Autoscaling & queueing: if customer enables auto-burst pool, we guarantee baseline capacity and best-effort additional nodes; financial credits apply only when baseline capacity is missed.

Acceptance test and reproducibility:
- We run joint acceptance: Redwood runs the canonical harness in your account (we provide the tools); you may run the same harness. We produce a test report (CSV + Grafana snapshot). If the pool meets thresholds, we mark the SLA as active.

I’ll attach a one-page test checklist to this thread. Happy to walk the infra team through the harness.

— Dylan Brooks

Lena — following up with an initial commercial proposal tied to the measurement plan Dylan described. Numbers below are illustrative; we can tighten after the acceptance test results.

Commit tiers (monthly equivalent of a 12-month reserved commit):
- Small (4xA100 equiv): list price $28k/month; 12mo commit = 15% discount; 24mo = 20%
- Mid (8xA100 equiv): list price $54k/month; 12mo commit = 18% discount; 24mo = 25%
- Large (16xA100 equiv): list price $100k/month; 12mo commit = 20% discount; 24mo = 28%

Pricing notes:
- Discounts tied to both term and baseline commit (we map tokens/sec to pool size).
- If you require strict financial SLAs (service credits triggered when baseline capacity missed), those are available at higher commit tiers and require an acceptance test run.
- We can offer an introductory concession for ACME: if you sign a 12-month mid-tier commit (8x equiv) within 21 days of our acceptance test, we can extend 18% + one month free as an onboarding credit.

Next steps for procurement:
- Execute SCO (statement of committed capacity) and attach the acceptance test report to the contract.
- Stephanie, can you confirm any standard indemnities or SLA language procurement will push back on?

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the numbers.

Marissa / team — quick legal checklist before we put SLAs in the contract:

1) Measurement windows and metrics: be explicit that metrics are computed using Redwood's measurement harness and jointly agreed workload traces. Include a reproducibility clause so customer may run the harness.
2) Exclusions: scheduled maintenance, force majeure, and any customer-induced misconfiguration (e.g., modifying model artifact mid-test) must be excluded.
3) Credit calculation: define credit as percentage of monthly fee for full baseline miss vs partial misses; also include cap (e.g., 50% of monthly fees).
4) Termination for repeated SLA failures: three failed months within rolling 12 months triggers remediation, not immediate termination.

I’ll add suggested contract language and circulate redlines. We should preserve the commercial concession but ensure acceptance test pass/fail is deterministic.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
